title: Evening Edition
notes: Evening Edition for Monday, Nov 2, 2026, the night before the U.S. midterm elections (Tuesday, Nov 3). It leads with the Supreme Court's election-eve decision on California's mail ballots. Stories already in the Morning Edition were not repeated; Trump's closing speech is an update to a morning story.
The U.S. has three stories tonight: the Supreme Court decision, Trump's closing speech and the New York City Marathon. Canada, Hong Kong and China have four each, and World has four.
Two stories have no photo because we found no suitable openly licensed image: the LNG Canada investment and Hong Kong's data-breach investigations.
Some stories rely on a single source (marked in Read more → Sources & checks); Caixin and RTHK's Chinese-language pages are summarized in translation.
provenance: The Supreme Court's own docket had not yet posted the order when we checked; the decision is reported by NPR and AP.
Mitsubishi Corporation's and AP's pages blocked our automated requests; that is an access limit, not a sign the pages are wrong.

stories.headline: Supreme Court turns down Trump administration's bid to make California set aside about 20,000 disputed mail ballots
stories.deck: On the eve of the midterms, the Supreme Court denied the Justice Department's emergency request to make California keep separate the mail ballots of more than 20,000 people the administration says are likely noncitizens. Lower courts had already refused.
stories.summary: On the eve of the midterms, the Supreme Court denied the Justice Department's emergency request to make California keep separate the mail ballots of more than 20,000 people the administration says are likely noncitizens. Lower courts had already refused. The department had sent California's secretary of state and Los Angeles County's top election official a list of about 20,000 registered voters it says are not citizens, and asked that their ballots be held back until citizenship could be verified. State and county officials questioned the list's accuracy and warned that eligible voters could be disenfranchised. On Oct 28, U.S. District Judge David Carter refused a temporary order, writing that voters must not lose a core right 'because of unfounded allegations stemming from a procedure rife with uncertainty and errors'. A divided 9th Circuit panel (2-1) also refused on Friday, Oct 30. Solicitor General D. John Sauer then asked the justices on Monday morning to order the ballots kept apart, arguing that once they are mixed in 'there is no way to get the challenged ballots back'. NPR and AP reported Monday evening that the court had denied the request.
stories.why: California has more than 23 million registered voters and had received over 6 million mail ballots by Sunday, CBS News reported. The ruling means ballots are processed under the state's normal rules while the underlying lawsuit continues.
stories.label: Reported + allegation
stories.note: As of our check, the Supreme Court's online docket listed only the application (filed Nov 2), not the order, and we had not seen the order's text, so we can't say whether any justices dissented. The noncitizen accusation is the administration's and has not been proven in court.

stories.headline: Trump's closing pitch at the Reflecting Pool: 20+ minutes on the renovation, then 'we gave this a very strong shot'
stories.deck: In his last scheduled speech before Election Day, President Trump spent more than 20 minutes on his renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and other Washington projects before turning to the midterms. He acknowledged that a sitting president's party usually loses midterms, adding: 'But we gave this a very strong shot.'
stories.summary: In his last scheduled speech before Election Day, President Trump spent more than 20 minutes on his renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and other Washington projects before turning to the midterms. He acknowledged that a sitting president's party usually loses midterms, adding: 'But we gave this a very strong shot.' Trump announced the pool's 'official opening' after a months-long, problem-plagued renovation the Guardian puts at $14 million, and repeated his claim that vandals caused damage that delayed it; CNBC notes the U.S. attorney for D.C. told a court in July that a contractor's botched installation was to blame. He called this 'the most important midterm, I believe, in our lifetime', attacked Michigan Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed by name and repeated his claim that 'everybody is going to get $5,000' if Republicans win. He also talked up a triumphal arch, a Potomac promenade and a planned 'National Garden of American Heroes'. CBS News, citing the University of Florida Voting Lab, says more than 57 million Americans had voted early.
stories.why: It's the president's final public argument before polls open Tuesday, Nov 3. His remark about midterm history is being read as preparing for possible Republican losses; the results will show how much it mattered.
stories.label: Reported + claim
stories.note: The vandalism explanation and the $5,000 promise are Trump's claims; the first is disputed by his own U.S. attorney's court statement, per CNBC.

stories.headline: Sweden's Andreas Almgren wins the NYC Marathon on his debut; Sheila Chepkirui takes her second women's title
stories.deck: Andreas Almgren pulled away from Italy's Yeman Crippa in Central Park to win Sunday's New York City Marathon in 2:06:01 — his first marathon. Kenya's Sheila Chepkirui out-sprinted defending champion Hellen Obiri to win the women's race in 2:24:36.
stories.summary: Andreas Almgren pulled away from Italy's Yeman Crippa in Central Park to win Sunday's New York City Marathon in 2:06:01 — his first marathon. Kenya's Sheila Chepkirui out-sprinted defending champion Hellen Obiri to win the women's race in 2:24:36. American Jessica McClain took second in 2:24:42, the first U.S. woman in the top three in New York since Shalane Flanagan in 2018, World Athletics said. Switzerland's Marcel Hug won the men's wheelchair race for a record eighth time and Catherine Debrunner won the women's wheelchair race. Organizers New York Road Runners say nearly 60,000 people ran, as the race marked 50 years of its five-borough course.
stories.why: The marathon is New York's biggest single-day sporting event, running through all five boroughs — including Brooklyn.
stories.label: Reported

stories.headline: Carney government's budget, due Thursday, is expected to include affordability measures and business tax incentives
stories.deck: Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne is scheduled to table the federal budget on Thursday, Nov 5. A senior government source told CBC News it will include new affordability measures, business tax incentives and spending on infrastructure, defence and culture.
stories.summary: Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne is scheduled to table the federal budget on Thursday, Nov 5. A senior government source told CBC News it will include new affordability measures, business tax incentives and spending on infrastructure, defence and culture. The source described three pillars — 'investing in the people, the identity and the growth of Canada' — and said Canadians can expect more detail on earlier announcements, including private investment in the country's four biggest airports, the promise to balance the operating budget a year early and the Canada Strong Fund, the sovereign wealth fund announced in April. Champagne has titled it 'Masters of Our Destiny' ('Maîtres chez nous'), a Quiet Revolution-era slogan.
stories.why: It will be Prime Minister Mark Carney's second budget, landing in the middle of the U.S. trade dispute and just as formal Canada-U.S. talks are expected to resume (see the Morning Edition).
stories.label: Reported + unnamed sources
stories.note: Nothing is final until the budget is tabled; details come from a source who was not authorized to speak publicly.

stories.headline: Six federal byelections set for Dec. 7 in Ontario, Quebec and Saskatchewan
stories.deck: Prime Minister Mark Carney has called byelections for Dec. 7 in six vacant ridings: three in Quebec, two in Ontario and one in Saskatchewan. CBC News says the races give the Liberals a chance to strengthen their thin majority in the House of Commons.
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney has called byelections for Dec. 7 in six vacant ridings: three in Quebec, two in Ontario and one in Saskatchewan. CBC News says the races give the Liberals a chance to strengthen their thin majority in the House of Commons. The ridings are Brantford—Brant South and Scarborough North (Ontario); Laurier—Sainte-Marie, Rosemont—La Petite-Patrie and Saint-Hyacinthe—Bagot—Acton (Quebec); and Yorkton—Melville (Saskatchewan). The Quebec seats were previously held by the Liberals, the NDP and the Bloc Québécois. Scarborough North's former Liberal MP Shaun Chen stepped down in August and later won a Toronto city council seat; Conservative Larry Brock resigned in Brantford—Brant South in September.
stories.why: Six seats at once is a meaningful test of the parties a year and a half after the last general election.
stories.label: Official statement + reported

stories.headline: Privacy watchdog investigates data breaches at Cathay, HK Airlines, YOHO and Broadway as scam losses top HK$1.5 million
stories.deck: Hong Kong's Privacy Commissioner has opened formal investigations into data-breach reports from airlines and electronics retailers, including Cathay Pacific, Hong Kong Airlines, Malaysia Airlines, YOHO and Broadway. It has received 51 complaints and 48 enquiries, with individual losses from about HK$10,000 to more than HK$1.5 million.
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Privacy Commissioner has opened formal investigations into data-breach reports from airlines and electronics retailers, including Cathay Pacific, Hong Kong Airlines, Malaysia Airlines, YOHO and Broadway. It has received 51 complaints and 48 enquiries, with individual losses from about HK$10,000 to more than HK$1.5 million. The watchdog warned of 'precision scams', where fraudsters use leaked flight or purchase details to pose as airline or shop staff offering refunds, returns or compensation. Real merchants won't ask for deposits, handling fees or transfers to 'verify' an account, it said; people should check through official websites, hotlines or stores before paying or sharing card details.
stories.why: Leaked booking details make scam calls sound convincing. Anyone who has flown or shopped with these firms should be wary of 'refund' calls.
stories.label: Official figures + reported
stories.note: The complaint and enquiry counts are as of Friday, Oct 30 (per RTHK).

stories.summary: The ICAC has charged William Fung Chi-wang, a former director of Johnson Cleaning Services and former CEO of its parent, and ex-general manager Jimmy Lee Sai-leung with conspiring to accept more than HK$75 million in bribes. The ICAC alleges the payments came from people including a supplier's owner, as a reward for favouring that supplier, from which Johnson bought fleets of cleaning vehicles and maintenance services worth over HK$160 million between November 2024 and January 2026. stories.headline: HKMA launches 'Project SAGE' to explore how AI agents could safely make payments and handle banking
stories.deck: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has launched Project SAGE ('Securing Agentic Finance with Governance and Enablement') and set up an expert group on 'agentic finance' — AI agents that act for customers. It's exploratory: use cases, verifying an agent's identity, standards and legal questions.
stories.summary: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has launched Project SAGE ('Securing Agentic Finance with Governance and Enablement') and set up an expert group on 'agentic finance' — AI agents that act for customers. It's exploratory: use cases, verifying an agent's identity, standards and legal questions. Example uses it lists include agent-driven shopping and everyday payments, business procurement and treasury, and machine-to-machine payments for digital services. It will also look at 'Know Your Agent' checks on an AI agent's identity and delegated authority, and at liability and consumer protection. The launch came during Hong Kong FinTech Week, where the HKMA also launched a post-quantum cryptography toolkit with HKUST.
stories.why: If AI assistants start paying bills and shopping for people, someone has to decide who's liable when they get it wrong. Hong Kong is trying to set those rules early.
stories.label: Official statement

stories.summary: The Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department marked 30 years of Hong Kong's marine parks by planting 30 corals at Hoi Ha Wan Marine Park with community members. The city now has eight marine parks and one marine reserve covering 8,517 hectares. More than 80 hard coral species — about a tenth of the world's total — have been recorded in Hong Kong waters, the department said. The first marine parks and reserve were set up in 1996, and the government says it is working to designate a Sharp Island Marine Park and expand protected areas.
stories.why: Hong Kong's coral diversity surprises many people; Hoi Ha Wan is one of the easiest places to snorkel and see it.

stories.headline: Wang Yi meets Iranian and Saudi security officials as Beijing steps up Middle East diplomacy
stories.deck: Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Iran's Ali Bagheri Kani on Monday that China supports Iran 'in safeguarding its own sovereignty and security' and urged all sides to seek a political solution 'rather than once again resorting to armed conflict'. He later met Saudi Arabia's national security adviser.
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Iran's Ali Bagheri Kani on Monday that China supports Iran 'in safeguarding its own sovereignty and security' and urged all sides to seek a political solution 'rather than once again resorting to armed conflict'. He later met Saudi Arabia's national security adviser. Bagheri Kani is deputy secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council; CNA says his Beijing visit hadn't been announced. Wang told Saudi adviser Musaad bin Mohammad al-Aiban that dialogue should end the conflict while protecting energy security and shipping lanes. China's foreign ministry also said its Middle East envoy, Zhai Jun, will visit Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia this month. The meetings came the same day as the Oman state visit covered in the Morning Edition, and days after President Trump threatened fresh strikes on Iran.
stories.why: China is Iran's biggest oil customer and depends on Gulf energy. Al Jazeera's Beijing correspondent says its diplomacy had stalled for weeks; this is a visible attempt to get back into the process.
stories.label: Reported + official statement
stories.note: Quotes come from Chinese government statements as reported by CNA and Al Jazeera; the interpretation of China's motives is the outlets' analysis.

stories.headline: Communist Party resolution puts loyalty first and widens scrutiny of officials' families and crypto-enabled graft
stories.deck: A Communist Party resolution on tightening internal discipline, released by Xinhua on Sunday, puts loyalty to the party front and centre and promises to keep up the anti-corruption campaign. Reuters reports it calls for closer checks on officials' family assets and on graft hidden through proxies, crypto and cross-border funds.
stories.summary: A Communist Party resolution on tightening internal discipline, released by Xinhua on Sunday, puts loyalty to the party front and centre and promises to keep up the anti-corruption campaign. Reuters reports it calls for closer checks on officials' family assets and on graft hidden through proxies, crypto and cross-border funds. The document, adopted at a leadership meeting last week, says officials should be vetted on their 'party spirit', including their conduct, social contacts and family values, and calls for routine checks on relatives' business activities. It tells members to safeguard Xi Jinping's status as the party's 'core'. Reuters notes it comes about a year before a leadership reshuffle at which Xi is expected to secure another five-year term.
stories.why: It sets the rules for China's vast officialdom ahead of next year's party congress, and signals how far Beijing's anti-graft drive will reach into officials' families.
stories.label: Reported + state media
stories.note: The resolution text was published by state news agency Xinhua; this summary relies on Reuters' reading of it, carried by Dawn.

stories.headline: China's October box office is the weakest in nearly a decade, Caixin reports
stories.deck: China's cinemas took in 2.046 billion yuan in October, the lowest October in close to ten years, according to Caixin, citing national film-fund data. Box office for the first nine months fell 29% from a year earlier, with more than 200 million fewer admissions.
stories.summary: China's cinemas took in 2.046 billion yuan in October, the lowest October in close to ten years, according to Caixin, citing national film-fund data. Box office for the first nine months fell 29% from a year earlier, with more than 200 million fewer admissions. Weekly takings have been under 200 million yuan for two weeks running (179 million yuan for Oct 26–Nov 1) for lack of new blockbusters. Caixin says the National Day holiday was weak and no big new release followed; three National Day films still made up 60% of last week's total. Cinema operators have taken the biggest hit, Caixin adds.
stories.why: China is one of the world's two biggest film markets, so a slump there matters for studios, including Hollywood, and for theatre chains.

stories.deck: Air China, China Eastern and China Southern all lost money in the first nine months of 2026 and are on track for full-year losses, according to analyst estimates compiled by LSEG. Jet fuel has more than doubled since U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran began in late February.
stories.summary: Air China, China Eastern and China Southern all lost money in the first nine months of 2026 and are on track for full-year losses, according to analyst estimates compiled by LSEG. Jet fuel has more than doubled since U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran began in late February. In the usually strong third quarter, Air China's net profit fell 92.6% to 270.6 million yuan and China Eastern's fell 98.2% to 64 million yuan, while China Southern swung to a 609 million yuan loss. Chinese airlines hedge less of their fuel than many peers, and domestic fares were weak amid competition including from high-speed rail. A BofA analyst expects losses to continue in the fourth quarter.
stories.why: It shows how the Iran war is feeding through to travel costs and company finances far from the Gulf.

stories.headline: Iliana Iotova wins Bulgaria's presidential runoff, becoming the country's first elected woman president
stories.deck: With all polling-station protocols counted, Bulgaria's Central Election Commission says Iliana Iotova and running mate Kiril Valchev won Sunday's runoff with 57.56% of the vote to 39.48% for Andrey Gyurov. Iotova, the incumbent, opposes military aid to Ukraine and favours dialogue with Russia.
stories.summary: With all polling-station protocols counted, Bulgaria's Central Election Commission says Iliana Iotova and running mate Kiril Valchev won Sunday's runoff with 57.56% of the vote to 39.48% for Andrey Gyurov. Iotova, the incumbent, opposes military aid to Ukraine and favours dialogue with Russia. Bulgarian National Radio says she is the country's seventh president and the first woman elected to the post. DW reports that the race between Iotova, who calls herself a 'president of peace', and the staunchly pro-European, pro-Ukraine former caretaker prime minister Gyurov turned into a referendum on foreign policy; Prime Minister Rumen Radev framed it as a choice 'between war and peace'.
stories.why: Bulgaria is an EU and NATO member on the Black Sea; its head of state's stance on Russia and Ukraine matters for European unity.

stories.note: Spellings vary: Bulgarian sources use Iotova, others Yotova.

stories.headline: More than 200 arrested in Germany as night-time violence follows mostly peaceful 'Gen Z' protests
stories.deck: Tens of thousands of young people marched in more than 30 German cities on Saturday for school funding and cost-of-living relief, and against plans to bring back compulsory military service. After dark, smaller radical groups clashed with police in Hamburg, Frankfurt, Berlin and Cologne; police reported more than 200 arrests.
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of young people marched in more than 30 German cities on Saturday for school funding and cost-of-living relief, and against plans to bring back compulsory military service. After dark, smaller radical groups clashed with police in Hamburg, Frankfurt, Berlin and Cologne; police reported more than 200 arrests. The daytime marches were organized by the campaign Gen Z regelt ('Gen Z takes charge'). In Frankfurt, masked groups not linked to the main protest looted shops, including a gun store, where at least two firearms were taken and later recovered, Anadolu reported. Hamburg police took 120 people into custody. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt called for 'harsh punishments' for rioters, the BBC reported; it notes similar youth-led protests in France, where more than 320,000 people marched the same day.
stories.why: Young people across Europe are protesting about living costs and military service. Germany's peaceful majority and its violent fringe are two separate stories.
stories.label: Reported + official statement + state media
stories.note: Arrest and Frankfurt details come from Anadolu, Turkey's state-run news agency, citing German police; the BBC independently reports the looting, clashes and the interior minister's comments.

stories.headline: Arsenal win at Anfield for the first time in 14 years and go top of the Premier League
stories.deck: Kai Havertz's first-half goal gave defending champions Arsenal a 1-0 win at Liverpool on Sunday, their first league victory at Anfield since 2012. Arsenal then held Liverpool without a shot on target to move back to the top of the table.
stories.summary: Kai Havertz's first-half goal gave defending champions Arsenal a 1-0 win at Liverpool on Sunday, their first league victory at Anfield since 2012. Arsenal then held Liverpool without a shot on target to move back to the top of the table. Havertz finished Declan Rice's low cross at the far post. Manager Mikel Arteta, who captained Arsenal the last time they won there, had told reporters beforehand that 'today has to be the day', the BBC reported; Arsenal had gone 16 trips to Anfield in all competitions without a win.
stories.why: One of English football's biggest fixtures, and a result that shapes the early title race.

stories.headline: Documenta 16 adds composer Raven Chacon and three curatorial advisers ahead of next summer's show in Kassel
stories.deck: Documenta, the influential contemporary art show held in Kassel, Germany, every five years, has added Pulitzer-winning composer Raven Chacon as curator-at-large and Osei Bonsu, Timea Junghaus and Noam Segal as curatorial advisers. The 16th edition is scheduled for June 12–Sept. 19, 2027, led by the Guggenheim's Naomi Beckwith.
stories.summary: Documenta, the influential contemporary art show held in Kassel, Germany, every five years, has added Pulitzer-winning composer Raven Chacon as curator-at-large and Osei Bonsu, Timea Junghaus and Noam Segal as curatorial advisers. The 16th edition is scheduled for June 12–Sept. 19, 2027, led by the Guggenheim's Naomi Beckwith. Beckwith's core team is Carla Acevedo-Yates, Romi Crawford, Mayra A. Rodríguez Castro and Xiaoyu Weng. Chacon, in 2022 the first Indigenous artist to win the Pulitzer Prize for Music, is known for the land-art installation Repellent Fence on the U.S.-Mexico border; Bonsu is a Tate Modern senior curator; Junghaus founded a Roma contemporary art space in Budapest; Segal is a Guggenheim associate curator. The 2022 edition was overshadowed by an antisemitism controversy.
stories.why: Documenta is one of the art world's most watched exhibitions. After the 2022 controversy, who runs the next one is closely followed.
